about.text: Tulum cheese is a traditional Turkish goat's milk cheese ripened in a goatskin casing, called tulum in Turkish.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: Goat’s traditionally; cow’s, sheep’s or buffalo blends commercially
PDO process: raw ewe's milk with rennet, pre-ripened about 10 days at 18–20 °C, then ripened at least 120 days at −2 to 0 °C in goatskin, salted with Kemah spring salt
Erzincan Tulum is a PDO; its sheep graze plateaus above 1,500 m

picks.why: The archetype: the Turkish sheep's-milk cheese matured in an animal-skin bag that gives the type its name.
Romania's best-known skin- or bark-packed sheep cheese, a staple of Carpathian shepherd tradition.
Croatia's PDO cheese ripened in a sheep-skin sack, the type's only protected name here.
A celebrated Central Anatolian tulum, matured in the natural limestone caves of Obruk plateau.
The defining sack-ripened cheese of Bosnia and Herzegovina, made by shepherds in Nevesinje and nearby highlands.
